signals.title: Bangladesh Bank tightens export-proceeds reporting
signals.summary: Exporters must repatriate proceeds within the prescribed period and report overdue amounts; enhanced monitoring applies to non-realization cases.
signals.raw_text:
Bangladesh Bank — Foreign Exchange Policy Department
FEPD-1 Circular No. 26
Date: 30 July 2026

Subject: Reporting and repatriation of export proceeds.

Authorized dealers and exporters are reminded that export proceeds must be repatriated within the period specified by Bangladesh Bank. The exporter undertakes to repatriate full proceeds of the export within the period specified by Bangladesh Bank in terms of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947.

Where proceeds are not repatriated within the prescribed period, the authorized dealer must report the outstanding amount and the reasons for delay to Bangladesh Bank. Enhanced monitoring applies to overdue export bills and cases of non-realization. Exporters should maintain a reconciliation of shipment, invoice, and repatriation records.

This is a demo excerpt based on public Bangladesh Bank export-trade guidance. Verify against the official circular and the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947.

metadata.quote: export proceeds must be repatriated within the period specified by Bangladesh Bank

signals.title: DHS expands UFLPA Entity List to 187 entities, including cotton and apparel
signals.summary: 43 companies were added. CBP applies a rebuttable presumption; cotton and garment supply chains face enhanced traceability scrutiny.
signals.raw_text:
Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act — Entity List update

On July 31, 2026, the United States added 43 companies based in China to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List. The newly listed entities are connected to the production and sale of goods made in Xinjiang or with the forced labor of Uyghurs and other groups specified in the UFLPA, and include cotton and garments. These additions bring the total number of entities on the UFLPA Entity List to 187.

CBP applies a rebuttable presumption that goods produced by listed entities are prohibited from entering the United States. Importers should maintain traceability documentation and respond to CBP requests.

This excerpt is a short quotation from public U.S. government material for the Chowkidar prototype.

metadata.quote: The newly listed entities are connected to the production and sale of goods made in Xinjiang or with the forced labor of Uyghurs and other groups specified in the UFLPA, and include cotton and garments.

signals.title: BIS revises the Entity List for a Hong Kong electronics distributor
signals.summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security amended the Export Administration Regulations by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under China.
signals.raw_text:
Revisions to the Entity List

In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

signals.title: EU forced-labour ban: implementation guidance ahead of 2027 application
signals.summary: Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 prohibits placing products made with forced labour on the EU market; authorities may request supply-chain evidence.
signals.raw_text:
Regulation (EU) 2024/3015 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2024 on prohibiting products made with forced labour on the Union market.

The Regulation prohibits economic operators from placing products made with forced labour on the Union market, making them available on the Union market, or exporting them from the Union market. It applies from 14 December 2027. Competent authorities may request information from economic operators about suspected forced labour.

This excerpt is a short quotation from the official text for the Chowkidar prototype.

risks.title: Supplier code and risk mapping are not yet aligned with CSDDD due diligence
risks.description: The supplier code predates the CSDDD transposition window. It does not require risk-based human rights and environmental due diligence, a grievance mechanism, or tier-2 mapping. The EU buyer's contract allows evidence requests and termination for uncured material breach.
risks.rationale: The obligation is in force for in-scope EU buyers and flows down the value chain. Padma has a policy commitment but no documented risk-based mapping or supplier grievance evidence. The gap is material to the Nordwear relationship and should be remediated before the next buyer audit.
